correctness.rationale: For the actual rates W_ij phi(delta f_i), symmetry makes the unweighted frequency M neutral harmonic. Differentiating the invertible mixed-state Dirichlet system gives the neutral occupation integral of L'_0 M; finite-state C² dependence gives the stated O(delta²) for fixed parameters. The cost drift is -(1/N) sum_a w_a(n_0-n_a)² and the neutral bracket rate is (2/N²) times that unsigned sum; the terminal Bernoulli variance therefore gives u_C=-(N-1)/(2N). The benefit drift uses n^T(D-W)Pn/N. Its row sums vanish; under the uniform singleton, the two-point function is (1-Pr(T_ij>t))/N, including the diagonal with T_ii=0. Integration gives u_B=-S/N² with the ordered leaf-pair sum as stated. To meet from (0,a) the lineages must cross edge a, at total hazard at most 2w_a. Conditional on no crossing there is positive probability to visit (b,a), b≠a, and stay there for a positive interval where the hazard is only w_a. The killed survival equation then gives mean first-crossing time strictly greater than 1/(2w_a). The leaf-pair first-step equation gives A_a+A_b-B_ab=(w_a A_a+w_b A_b-1)/(w_a+w_b)>0. Thus the diagonal contribution to S already exceeds 1 and all remaining terms are positive. Complementing flips the payoff up to a constant, whose contribution to L'_0 M is zero; it doubles the fixation slope in the paired difference. N≥3, uniform initial placement, strict positivity of every w_a and weak selection are essential to the stated analysis; it is not a finite-selection or uniform-in-weights assertion.
